results.hidden_info_read: only the 16 own-deck aggregates (truth = own deck, which leaks the contents of own face-down life). Opponent aggregates read the unseen pool (hand+deck+face-down life) as a set only = invariant under every world sample.

proposal_v15.recommended: A: replace the 16 own-deck columns with the information-set expectation (known-in-deck cards counted exactly + unknown cards of (deck ∪ face-down life) prorated by the deck's share of unknown slots; apex = max over that pool). Same shape/position/scale as v14 -> r13d reads it unchanged. Cost: Rust scalars.rs + tokens.rs, Python encoder.py + n_rel_feat.py, oracle update, ENC_VERSION 15; old waves cannot be re-encoded (records hold no board) -> waves 48+ switch, full turnover in 2 waves under the current windows. Expected strength gain small (value jitter ~0.005 mean, 0.013 in turns 0-2).
not_recommended: B: add known-card features (opp hand known 4.9% of points, deck top 4.7%)
C: drop the 16 columns (only as a control; can be trained on existing waves now)

notes: rs_enc_v14_probe.py compares decide outputs and latency, it does not enumerate features. The feature list was taken from the column table at the top of rust/opcg_engine/src/encode/scalars.rs and n_rel_feat.S_COLS / R_COLS / EXTRA_COLS (Python<->Rust column parity is what rs_encode_oracle.py checks).

To measure exactly what the search feeds the net, a measurement-only pyo3 hook Game.encode_world was added (rebuilding the world with the same sampler and the same Pcg32SearchRng(search_seed + i) as decide's world i). It changes no existing behaviour; make test is green on the final tree.
Token-state features are bundled per zone (own_leader/own_field/hand/opp_leader/opp_field x 22 columns); rel per R column. A difference in any slot of the bundle counts.

The instrument's first version merged the two opp_pool_big columns by name; it was fixed (second gets '#2') and the main run was repeated (identical games, identical changed rows). The side 160-sim run was made with the first version (both opp-pool columns are invariant anyway).
Leaf (in-tree) inputs were not measured: under peek, draws inside the tree took the real next card, which is a search-side leak (handled by rs-fair), not an encoding one.
The Python board has no known_by; a Python mirror of proposal A matches Rust only on boards with no known cards until a hook passes known_by.
